1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Bc5 4.c3 Nf6 5.d.strategy: Rebuilds the broad pawn centre and attacks the bishop with tempo. White gets space and an open game; the price is that the bishop's check on b4 interrupts the build-up and the e4-pawn must be defended against the knight on f6.
1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Bc5 4.c3 Nf6 5.d.name: Italian Game: Classical Variation, Greco Gambit, Traditional Line
1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Bc5 4.c3 Nf6 5.d.background: The old main line of the Giuoco Piano, developed by Gioachino Greco in the early 17th century.

1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Bc5 4.c3 Nf6 5.d.strategy: Drives the knight away at once and gains space, leaving the recapture on d4 for later. White gets the initiative only if Black fails to strike back in the centre immediately; if it does, White keeps more space and Black has active pieces.
1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Bc5 4.c3 Nf6 5.d.name: Italian Game: Classical Variation, Greco Gambit, Modern Line
1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Bc5 4.c3 Nf6 5.d.background: A line favoured by Evgeny Sveshnikov, which has seen a surge in popularity in the early 21st century.

1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Bc5 4.c3 Nf6 5.d.strategy: A gambit: White does not recapture, but attacks the bishop with the b-pawn and threatens to chase the knight with b5. It aims for quick development and open lines in return for a pawn. Sharp, and Black must take care not to fall behind in development.
1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Bc5 4.c3 Nf6 5.d.name: Italian Game: Classical Variation, Greco Gambit, Dubov Italian
1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Bc5 4.c3 Nf6 5.d.background: A gambit advocated by Daniil Dubov. In the 21st century it has emerged as a frequent alternative to 6.e5 and 6.cxd4.

1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Bc5 4.c3 Nf6 5.d.strategy: A gambit: White castles without recapturing and lets Black take the e4-pawn as well. Black can accept it safely and keeps the extra pawn after White recaptures on d4; White's lead in development is the only compensation, and it is not enough.
1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Bc5 4.c3 Nf6 5.d.name: Italian Game: Scotch Gambit, Walbrodt-Baird Gambit
1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Bc5 4.c3 Nf6 5.d.background: A rarely seen gambit that was more popular in the era of Romantic chess.

1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Bc5 4.c3 Nf6 5.d.strategy: Saves the bishop with check, so White must react before it can attend to e4, which the knight attacks. Retreating to b6 instead lets White push e5 and drive the knight away with a gain of space, which is why the check is the standard way to meet the recapture.

Strikes back in the centre at once: the pawn attacks the bishop, so White has to deal with that before anything else. The knight reaches a strong square on e4, Black's pieces become active, and White keeps more space. The only good answer to the push.
1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Bc5 4.c3 Nf6 5.d.name: Italian Game: Classical Variation, Greco Gambit, Modern Line

1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Bc5 4.c3 Nf6 5.d.strategy: Runs the knight forward and into a trap: the bishop lands on d5 and the knight has no safe retreat. Black must prop it up with the f-pawn, which weakens the king's side, or sacrifice it for a speculative attack. White keeps the better chances either way.
